Nerve conduction studies; electromyogram; genetics; CK

diagnostic_tests_recommendations.1: Electrocardiogram (ECG). A normal ECG makes the diagnosis of HF unlikely. The ECG may reveal abnormalities such as AF, Q waves, LV hypertrophy (LVH), and a widened QRS complex that increase the likelihood of a diagnosis of HF and may guide therapy.
diagnostic_tests_recommendations.2: Measurement of NPs recommended if available. BNP <35 pg/mL, NT-proBNP <125 pg/mL, or MR-proANP <40 pmol/L make a diagnosis of HF unlikely.
diagnostic_tests_recommendations.3: Basic investigations: serum urea and electrolytes, creatinine, full blood count, liver and thyroid function tests to differentiate HF from other conditions, provide prognostic information, and guide therapy.
diagnostic_tests_recommendations.4: Echocardiography recommended as key investigation for assessment of cardiac function and other parameters (chamber size, LVH pattern, regional wall motion abnormalities suggesting CAD, Takotsubo syndrome, or myocarditis; RV function; pulmonary hypertension; valvular function; diastolic function).
diagnostic_tests_recommendations.5: Chest X-ray recommended to investigate other potential causes of breathlessness (e.g., pulmonary disease) and may provide supportive evidence of HF (pulmonary congestion or cardiomegaly).
